answer.topic_label: Stock return momentum in Imperial Russia
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the abstract-based fields are inferred.

answer.topic_label: Unvested equity pay and CEO retention
answer.notes: FAS 123-R is an accounting standard from FASB, a private standard-setter recognised by the SEC; it is treated as policy, and the CEO departures it set off are coded as an unintended consequence.

answer.topic_label: Paternity leave quota and couple separation
answer.notes: Heterogeneity by traditional family constellations is only implied, so impacts_on_specific_groups is a borderline yes.

answer.topic_label: Climate disasters, salience and bank loan pricing
answer.notes: Uses disaster shocks to borrowers who were at risk but not directly hit to identify how banks update loan pricing; it studies no government policy.

answer.topic_label: One-Child Policy effects on life-cycle outcomes
answer.notes: The study's identification comes from differences in penalty strictness across provinces and over time. I coded unintended consequences and group impacts as yes because of the effects on co-residence with the elderly and on female empowerment, but that is a judgement call.

answer.topic_label: Long-run effects of WWII-era management training
answer.notes: The abstract does not name its identification strategy; I inferred a quasi-experimental design from the comparison among program applicants.

answer.topic_label: Letter grade effects on earnings and course choice
answer.notes: Treating a university's coarse letter-grading system as policy is a judgement call; the behavioural response in later course choice is coded as an unintended consequence.

answer.topic_label: Soap opera financial education in South Africa
answer.notes: I coded the financial education intervention, scripted into a TV soap opera, as a programme being evaluated. It is unclear whether a public body set it, as the policy definition requires.

answer.topic_label: Measuring US top 1 percent income shares
answer.notes: The paper adjusts for tax reforms only as a measurement issue and does not evaluate them; I coded the Joint Committee on Taxation as economics because it is a tax-analysis unit, though that call is uncertain.

answer.topic_label: Firm-specific productivity and cross-country income gaps
answer.notes: I coded this as a development-accounting measurement paper with no specific policy, so descriptive_fact is a marginal yes. Authors 2 and 3 are coded economics from their NBER affiliation, and author 1 from the IDB as a development-bank economics unit.

answer.topic_label: CIA vaccine ruse and immunization in Pakistan
answer.notes: I treated the CIA's use of a fake vaccination campaign as a government action, so the drop in immunization counts as an unintended consequence; the effect is identified through differences between districts with more or less Islamist support.

answer.topic_label: Lottery windfalls and incumbent vote share
answer.notes: The lottery is a natural experiment, not a policy under study; author 1 coded economics through the IZA affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Danish immigrants spreading dairy knowledge in America
answer.notes: Author 1's unit is a combined Department of Business and Economics, coded economics.

answer.topic_label: China's housing boom, vacancies and bubble risk
answer.notes: This JEP piece is a descriptive analysis of China's housing market rather than a literature survey, so it is coded as a research article; the policy discussion of curtailing supply is speculative.

answer.topic_label: Cautious expectations from estimating information weights
answer.notes: The consumption-savings application may be a quantitative illustration compared with evidence, but the paper is mainly theoretical.

answer.topic_label: Dealer markups and pricing in municipal bonds
answer.notes: The abstract does not say how the impact of the MSRB rules was identified; author 3's affiliation field is cluttered with acknowledgement text but names McCombs School of Business.

answer.topic_label: Credit rating agency market power and rating standards
answer.notes: The main cross-country result is correlational. Quasi-experimental identification comes from the NRSRO designation of local Japanese rating agencies, which is a regulatory action that raised competition and led to more inflated ratings.

answer.topic_label: CBT-style youth programs reducing crime and dropout
answer.notes: The affiliation text is garbled and shared across all authors, so I used only each author's last unit. Author 3's "School of Education and Social Policy" could also be coded as other (education). I treated the nonprofit school-based program and the program in the public detention center as public programmes.

answer.topic_label: Optimal monetary policy during debt deleveraging at ZLB
answer.notes: The abstract describes a theoretical New Keynesian model of optimal policy and mentions no data. Stockholm School of Economics is coded as economics because of its name and the author's CEPR affiliation.

answer.topic_label: COVID-19 economic impacts in low-income countries
answer.notes: Survey article; the policy categories describe the research it reviews rather than any new analysis. Author 2 has a joint management and economics affiliation and is coded as economics.

answer.topic_label: International students in US higher education
answer.notes: This is a JEP synthesis that touches on visa policy only as a mediating factor; author 2 is at the Urban Institute with no unit named.

answer.topic_label: Drivers of high cement prices in Africa
answer.notes: The abstract says only that policy implications are discussed and studies no specific policy. Author 2 is coded economics because of the CEPR and BREAD affiliations, since no LSE department is named.

answer.topic_label: Price expectations and the US housing boom
answer.notes: Choosing between structural and descriptive for the sign-restricted SVAR was a judgement call; author 1 was coded economics on the strength of the NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Investor disagreement dynamics, momentum and long-term reversal
answer.notes: Author 1 is listed under both a business school and NBER and was coded economics because NBER is named; the paper may use a model to infer beliefs from returns, so the line between empirical and structural work is uncertain.

answer.topic_label: Co-inventor death and team-specific capital
answer.notes: Identification comes from inventors' premature deaths, used as a natural experiment; no policy is studied.

answer.topic_label: Output losses after financial crises in OECD
answer.notes: New narrative dataset on financial distress; no specific policy is studied.

answer.topic_label: Lucas Prize award for top inequality paper
answer.notes: This is a prize announcement summarising a prize-winning paper (Jones and Kim on top income inequality), and no authors are listed.

answer.topic_label: Rising health care needs of aging US prisoners
answer.notes: Harsh sentencing is mentioned only as background, not studied as a specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Probability distributions for realized covariance matrices
answer.notes: This is a methods paper that also has an empirical part comparing fit and forecasts; I coded the design as not_empirical because the data work is there to evaluate the new distributions.

answer.topic_label: Book review: democracy and monetary policy
answer.notes: Book review in JEL; the listed author is the reviewer (Duke Law), not the book's author.

answer.topic_label: Women directors' expertise and board value
answer.notes: AER Papers and Proceedings-style short paper; mechanisms concern board diversity rather than a public policy, so identifies_mechanisms is coded no.

answer.topic_label: Great Migration and Black upward mobility in North
answer.notes: Uses a shift-share design on migration shocks, not a policy; policing appears only as a possible mechanism. It speaks to 'moving to opportunity' policy only by implication.

answer.topic_label: Policy diffusion and partisan polarization across states
answer.notes: Studies adoption of 602 existing state policies, not their effects; author 1 coded economics on the strength of the NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Consumer privacy and price discrimination in market segmentation
answer.notes: The platform design problem is a firm strategy, not a public policy. The paper's link to the privacy debate is only implied, so all policy categories are coded no. Author 2 is coded economics on the strength of the Paris School of Economics affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Automaker collusion against emissions regulation
answer.notes: Coding unintended consequences and mechanisms as yes is a judgement call: it reads the firms' joint evasion of the emissions regulation as an unintended behavioural response.

answer.topic_label: Accrual-based top income shares using Norwegian ownership data
answer.notes: Mainly a measurement paper; author 3 lists both Columbia SIPA and NBER and was coded economics because of the NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Emotional protests, fairness and public debt policy
answer.notes: The paper is mainly a theory of how unrest shapes policy; the abstract describes its supporting evidence only briefly, as "consistent with" the model.

answer.topic_label: NSF rotators' mentoring spillovers on junior scientists
answer.notes: Design inferred as quasi-experimental from the timing of the rotator's return and the comparison with control groups; the effects on colleagues are coded as spillovers of the NSF rotation programme.

answer.topic_label: Corporate finance framing of sovereign debt and money
answer.notes: This is a presidential address, coded as a research article because it presents an original theoretical framework; the welfare category rests on its discussion of the costs and benefits of inflation and optimal reserves.

answer.topic_label: Teacher pay-for-performance selection and effort in Rwanda
answer.notes: The pay-for-performance contract was set up for the experiment, so I coded it as a proposed policy rather than an existing one; author 3's School of International Development is coded as other.

answer.topic_label: Factor momentum explains stock return momentum
answer.notes: Author 2 coded as business school only from the Tuck Hall address and tuck email domain; author 1 has no affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Student debt cancellation and racial wealth gaps
answer.notes: The paper simulates a proposed relief plan that was never carried out, by mechanically applying relief to wealth data rather than estimating a causal effect.

answer.topic_label: Export demand shocks and firm innovation
answer.notes: Identification relies on exogenous firm-level export demand shocks, which looks like a shift-share design. Author 1 is coded economics because of the PSE and LSE affiliations, and author 4 because of NBER.

answer.topic_label: Minimum grade rules for economics majors
answer.notes: The 'policy' is a college's academic rule rather than a government policy, so the policy categories were applied loosely; the 6% fall in majors was coded as an unintended effect.

answer.topic_label: Bootstrap standard errors and conservative inference
JPE editorial turnaround time statistics
answer.notes: Journal front matter: a table of editorial decision times; the abstract field holds scraped page text, and no authors are listed.

answer.topic_label: Multinationals transmitting business cycle shocks across countries
answer.notes: Combines firm-level comovement facts with a calibrated quantitative model; no policy is studied.

answer.topic_label: Manipulability of stable mechanisms in large matching markets
answer.notes: The abstract does not tie the paper to any particular public matching program, so all policy categories are coded no.

answer.topic_label: Economic epidemiology: behavior, disease dynamics, policy
answer.notes: This is a survey, so the policy categories describe the work it reviews (models of interventions, externalities, heterogeneity), not new results of its own.

answer.topic_label: Car spending collapse in the Great Recession
answer.notes: No policy is studied; descriptive_fact is coded yes for the cohort-level facts on car spending from CEX data, while the main contribution is structural inference about which shocks caused the recession.

answer.topic_label: Contingent convertible debt design and bank capital structure
answer.notes: I treated contingent convertible debt as a proposed regulatory capital instrument. Whether the paper counts as policy-relevant is uncertain, because the abstract frames it mainly as a question of how firms structure their capital.

answer.topic_label: Childhood conflict exposure and asylum seeker crime
answer.notes: Author 2's unit is the Geneva School of Economics and Management, which combines economics and management, so economics is uncertain; the policy evidence comes from differences in integration policies across Swiss regions, which is weaker identification than the cohort-exposure design.

answer.topic_label: Earnings reporting responses to pension benefit formulas
answer.notes: Author 1 was coded as economics because their email domain points to UDELAR's economics institute (iecon). Authors 2 and 3 were coded as economics because of their CEPR and IZA affiliations. The identification design is not stated explicitly; it is inferred from responses around the benefit calculation window.

answer.topic_label: Teacher student loan forgiveness take-up and value
answer.notes: Combines quasi-experimental eligibility variation with an RCT information intervention; coded experimental, but the two designs carry similar weight.

answer.topic_label: Idea exchange, city size and skill premia
answer.notes: The model is checked against established facts about cities, but the abstract does not describe any estimation, so I coded it as theoretical.

answer.topic_label: Nonparametric bootstrap for yield curve inference
answer.notes: The paper is mainly about method; its empirical application looks at whether bond returns can be predicted.

answer.topic_label: Credit supply shocks and firms' output pricing
answer.notes: The shock studied is the Lehman Brothers failure, a market event rather than a policy, so all policy categories are coded no even though the paper identifies mechanisms (inventory and liquidity).

answer.topic_label: Bayesian social learning in networks about changing state
answer.notes: Third author is at a private firm (Uber), coded other.

answer.topic_label: Market value of FinTech patent innovations
answer.notes: The paper uses stock price responses to patent filings to measure value, an event-study-style method, but it studies firm innovation rather than any policy.

answer.topic_label: Economic research on what managers do
answer.notes: This is mainly a review, with some descriptive analysis of managers' skills as listed on LinkedIn.

answer.topic_label: Lockdown curfews and elderly mental health in Turkey
answer.notes: The headline result is a mental health side effect of a COVID curfew, so the primary category is unintended consequences; causal effect of policy is also marked yes.

answer.topic_label: Childhood coca labor and adult criminality in Peru
answer.notes: US antidrug policy timing is used as identifying variation, and the paper treats the resulting child labor and crime as spillovers; the conditional cash transfer rollout is studied as a mitigating policy.

answer.topic_label: Book review: economic crises and globalization
answer.notes: This is a book review in JEL, so it is coded as non-research.

answer.topic_label: Unilateral divorce laws and assortative marriage matching
answer.notes: Combines staggered-adoption policy variation with an estimated structural equilibrium model; headline coded as quasi-experimental, though the structural part is substantial.

answer.topic_label: Identification and normalizations in skill formation models
answer.notes: Identification theory paper; unclear from the abstract whether it includes an empirical application.

answer.topic_label: German Reunification shock and East German youths' college plans
answer.notes: I treated Reunification as a system-wide regime shock, not a targeted policy, so all policy categories are coded no; this is a judgement call.

answer.topic_label: Test power in second-order identified GMM models
High-dimensional network model of social media influencers
answer.notes: Author 2 lists many units (blockchain centre, information science and finance, mathematics, economics institute), so economics is a judgement call; the StockTwits application only illustrates the method.

answer.topic_label: Law enforcement, managerial delegation and aggregate productivity
answer.notes: Law enforcement is treated as an institutional quality parameter; the counterfactuals vary it in a quantitative GE model, so whether it counts as 'policy' is a judgement call.

answer.topic_label: India's growth path and development shortfalls
answer.notes: A JEP essay that pulls together descriptive evidence on India's development rather than presenting new causal research.

answer.topic_label: Optimal spatial allocation of cognitive workers across cities
answer.notes: The optimal spatial policy is derived inside the model as a planner's allocation; no existing policy is evaluated.

answer.topic_label: Corporate flexibility and firm plans during COVID
answer.notes: The COVID shock is used as a source of variation, but the design reads as correlational analysis of CFO survey data rather than a clear causal design, and no specific policy is studied.

answer.topic_label: Incidence of business owner taxes on employees
answer.notes: Pass-through to workers treated as an unintended consequence; the author is at a business school and no finer unit is named.

answer.topic_label: Norwegian vocational education reform and social mobility
answer.notes: Authors were coded as economics because each lists an NBER affiliation; the University of Chicago is given without a named department.

answer.topic_label: Left-behind classmates' effects on children's personality traits
answer.notes: Identification comes from random assignment of pupils to classrooms, which is a natural experiment, not a policy evaluation; author 2's digital humanities and computational social science unit was coded as other.

answer.topic_label: Optimal monetary policy and asset price overshooting
answer.notes: Author 2's affiliation field is a garbled acknowledgment naming MIT/NBER, Yale SOM, and CEPR; coded as economics on the basis of NBER/CEPR.

answer.topic_label: Bank regulation and capital flow surges and stops
answer.notes: The paper asks about policy effects, but the abstract reports associations ('correlated'), so I did not code it as causal.

answer.topic_label: Seed quality uncertainty and farmer returns in Tanzania
answer.notes: The experiment varies seed quality and what farmers know about it, not a government policy. Its relevance to policy (seed quality regulation) is only implied, so the channel finding about labour was not coded as a policy mechanism.

answer.topic_label: Church attendance effects on petty crime
answer.notes: The paper looks at church attendance, not a government policy, so all policy categories are coded no.

answer.topic_label: Dynamic bank deposit management and leverage regulation
answer.notes: Theory paper; the link to leverage regulation is brief, and author 2's affiliation text is a correspondence address.

answer.topic_label: WTO versus preferential trade agreements
answer.notes: Survey with a normative judgement on the WTO versus PTAs, coded as a welfare evaluation; authors 1 and 3 coded economics because of their NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Nineteenth-century mechanization and task-level labor productivity
answer.notes: The paper appeared in JEP but analyses a historical dataset itself, so it is coded as original research rather than a survey.

answer.topic_label: Inside collateral pyramids and financial fragility
answer.notes: Treasuries as outside collateral are mentioned, but the paper does not analyse any specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Financial sanctions and German bank cross-border lending
answer.notes: The abstract does not state the identifying variation, so quasi_experimental is inferred from how sanctions are imposed across countries; author 3 is coded economics because of the CESifo affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Seven centuries of long-maturity real interest rates
answer.notes: Author 3 has two affiliations (Boston College finance department and the Hoover Institution); coded by the named department, finance.

answer.topic_label: Gender earnings gap widening over the lifecycle
answer.notes: Author 4's Institute for Social Research is a multidisciplinary social science institute; coded as sociology_demography with uncertainty.

answer.topic_label: Unemployment versus negative equity in mortgage default
answer.notes: The abstract includes editorial submission boilerplate; the default estimates come from PSID household data with no stated identification strategy.

answer.topic_label: Gender differences in student professional networking usage
answer.notes: The descriptive_fact code is a judgement call: the paper documents a gender gap that matters for policy, but it does not study any policy.

answer.topic_label: Audit distortions in Chilean public procurement
answer.notes: IDB coded as economics by analogy with World Bank research; GRIPS coded as public policy; author 3 coded economics because of the CEPR affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Monetary tightening, mortgage credit and distributional effects
answer.notes: The identification seems to come from DTI underwriting thresholds and regional exposure, but the abstract doesn't say so outright. Author 1 is at a housing regulator (FHFA), coded as other; authors 2 and 4 also list NBER, but their business-school unit was used.

answer.topic_label: Contrast effects in sequential interview evaluations
answer.notes: The proposed changes to interview design are aimed at organisations' admission and hiring processes, and the abstract does not say a public body sets them, so all policy categories are coded no.

answer.topic_label: Mental health spillovers among new mothers
answer.notes: The paper estimates peer spillovers that arise within a public postnatal group programme, not the programme's own effect, so it is coded as an unintended consequence. VIVE is a multidisciplinary social science centre, so its authors' discipline is coded unknown.

answer.topic_label: Private equity buyouts and workplace injury rates
answer.notes: The abstract compares outcomes before and after buyouts without naming the identifying design, so the design could be quasi-experimental (event study or DiD); PE buyouts are firm actions, not policy.

answer.topic_label: Firm dynamics with on-the-job search frictions
answer.notes: The abstract does not make clear whether the quantitative model is estimated or calibrated, so structural is a judgement call; author 2 has NBER/CEPR affiliations but was coded by their Stern School unit.

answer.topic_label: Removing sterilization requirement for legal gender change
answer.notes: The design is a before/after comparison around Sweden's 2013 reform, so the causal coding is borderline. The Swedish Institute for Social Research is a multidisciplinary unit, so it was coded as other.

answer.topic_label: Government portfolio choice over risky public programs
answer.notes: Theory-only model that judges how attractive stylised financial stability programs are; it does not look at any specific existing program.

answer.topic_label: Racial disparities in small business loan terms
answer.notes: The Public Policy Institute of California is coded as public policy because the institute itself focuses on that one field; the other affiliations name only a university.

answer.topic_label: Optimal inflation with incomplete markets and money bubbles
answer.notes: Theoretical model evaluating the welfare effects of the money growth/inflation rate in general; no specific real-world policy is studied.

answer.topic_label: Foreign monetary policy spillovers to U.S. Treasury yields
answer.notes: I treated the effect of ECB policy on U.S. yields as a cross-border spillover, so I coded it as an unintended consequence rather than as the policy's intended causal effect.

answer.topic_label: Movie role model effects on Ugandan students' exams
answer.notes: The researcher ran the movie screening, not a public body; I treated it as a possible education intervention, so the policy codes are a judgement call.

answer.topic_label: Mutual fund managers' attention over the business cycle
answer.notes: Author 1's Imperial unit is a combined accounting/finance/macroeconomics group (plus CEPR), so I coded it as finance_accounting; author 3 also lists NBER but the named unit is Columbia Business School.

answer.topic_label: Unvested equity pay and CEO retention
answer.notes: FAS 123-R is a private-board (FASB) accounting standard used mainly as a source of variation to study firms' vesting choices, so all policy categories are coded no; borderline because the abstract calls it a regulatory change.

answer.topic_label: Swedish paternity leave reform and couple separation
answer.notes: The reform's intended effect is higher take-up of fathers' leave and its side effect is more separations. The mechanism is argued from restrictiveness and role conflict, not cleanly identified.

answer.topic_label: China's one-child policy and life-cycle outcomes
answer.notes: Lower fertility counts as the intended effect; education, marriage, living with elderly relatives and female empowerment are coded as outcomes outside the policy's aims.

answer.topic_label: Climate disasters, salience and bank loan spreads
answer.notes: Identification uses natural disasters as event shocks with indirectly exposed borrowers, which is a design but not a policy; the design coding is a judgement call.

answer.topic_label: Long-run and spillover effects of WWII management training
answer.notes: The abstract doesn't name the identifying variation; I coded the design as quasi-experimental because the sample is a panel of program applicants.

answer.topic_label: Letter grade effects on earnings and course choice
answer.notes: The paper studies a university grading rule, which the codebook does not count as a policy, so every policy category is no.

answer.topic_label: Financial education via TV soap opera
answer.notes: The abstract doesn't say who ran the soap-opera financial education campaign, so treating it as a public intervention is uncertain.

answer.topic_label: Measuring US top 1 percent income shares
answer.notes: The Joint Committee on Taxation was coded as economics because it is a tax-analysis staff, but that call is uncertain. Tax reforms come up only as a measurement adjustment.

answer.topic_label: Multinational firm productivity and cross-country income gaps
answer.notes: IDB affiliation names no unit and was coded economics as a development bank; authors 2 and 3 were coded economics because of their NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: CIA vaccine ruse and immunization in Pakistan
answer.notes: The paper studies a covert CIA operation and the propaganda that followed it, so under the codebook it is a one-off event rather than a policy and every policy category is coded no.

answer.topic_label: Danish immigrants spreading dairy knowledge in US
answer.notes: Author 1 is in a combined Department of Business and Economics, coded as economics; the paper studies historical migration, not a policy.

answer.topic_label: Cautious expectations from estimating information weights
answer.notes: The consumption-savings application reads as an illustration of the theory, not an estimation, so I coded the paper as theoretical.

answer.topic_label: Lottery windfalls and votes for incumbents
answer.notes: The lottery winnings are an exogenous income shock used as a natural experiment, not a policy being evaluated; author 1 is coded economics because of the IZA affiliation, and author 2's affiliation gives no unit.

answer.topic_label: China's housing boom and bubble risk
answer.notes: I coded this JEP piece as a descriptive research article, not a survey; the abstract only discusses government supply policy in general terms.

answer.topic_label: Credit rating agency market power and rating standards
answer.notes: The NRSRO designation of Japanese local CRAs is a regulatory action, but the paper uses it only as a source of variation in market power, not as a policy whose effects are studied; the main cross-country results are correlational.

answer.topic_label: Dealer markups and pricing in municipal bonds
answer.notes: The abstract says MSRB rules had limited impact on markups but gives no identifying design, so I coded it as descriptive; the affiliation fields are jumbled and may not line up with the listed authors.

answer.topic_label: Cognitive behavioural programmes reducing youth crime and dropout
answer.notes: BAM was developed by a nonprofit but delivered in public schools and a county detention centre, so it is treated as a public programme. The affiliation strings are pooled across authors, so most authors are coded unknown; author 3's School of Education and Social Policy is coded other (education).

answer.topic_label: Optimal monetary policy at ZLB with deleveraging
answer.notes: Author 3 is coded economics because of the CEPR affiliation, since the Stockholm School of Economics names no unit; the abstract does not say whether the model is calibrated.

answer.topic_label: COVID-19 economic effects in low-income countries
answer.notes: Survey article; causal_effect_of_policy reflects the reviewed evidence on policy responses rather than the authors' own estimates. The pandemic itself is treated as a shock, not a policy.

answer.topic_label: International students in US higher education
answer.notes: JEP survey; visa policy is mentioned only as a mediating factor, not studied; author 2 is coded from the Urban Institute, a policy think tank, and the affiliation names no unit.

answer.topic_label: Cement prices, markups and market size in Africa
answer.notes: The abstract says only that "policy implications are discussed" and names no specific policy, so policy_reference is none.

answer.topic_label: Team-specific capital among US patent inventors
answer.notes: The paper uses inventors' premature deaths as natural shocks, so no policy is studied; the Treasury Office of Tax Analysis author is coded as economics.

answer.topic_label: Probability distributions for realized covariance matrices
answer.notes: This is a methods paper. Its empirical part only compares how well each distribution fits the data and forecasts out of sample, so the design is coded not_empirical.

answer.topic_label: Output losses after financial crises in OECD countries
answer.notes: The paper builds a new dataset of financial distress and documents facts about what follows crises; it studies no specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Rising health care needs of aging US prisoners
answer.notes: Harsh sentencing is mentioned only as background; the paper does not evaluate any specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Great Migration racial shocks and Black upward mobility
answer.notes: Shift-share design applied to a migration shock rather than a policy; policing appears only as a possible mechanism, not as a policy being evaluated.

answer.topic_label: Lucas Prize award for top income inequality paper
answer.notes: Prize announcement that summarises the winning paper (Jones and Kim); no authors listed; the abstract field includes webpage boilerplate.

answer.topic_label: Book review: democracy and monetary policy
answer.notes: Book review in JEL; coded non_research.

answer.topic_label: Consumer privacy, market segmentation and price discrimination
answer.notes: The paper studies how a private platform designs its search interface rather than a public policy; I coded author 2 as economics because the Paris School of Economics affiliation is specific to economics.

answer.topic_label: Women directors' expertise and corporate board value
answer.notes: Board composition is a firm decision and the abstract names no diversity mandate, so every policy category is no; this looks like a short proceedings-style paper.

answer.topic_label: Partisan polarization and policy diffusion across U.S. states
answer.notes: The paper describes how 602 state policies were adopted and spread; it does not estimate what those policies did. Author 1 is coded economics because of the NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Automaker collusion to evade emissions regulation
answer.notes: The welfare loss is attributed to firm collusion, not to a policy. The policy-design counterfactuals are inferred from the abstract's final sentence.

answer.topic_label: Emotional protests, fairness, and public debt policy
answer.notes: The paper is mainly theoretical, with only a brief empirical check ("evidence is consistent"). It explains how unrest shapes policy rather than studying the effects of a policy.

answer.topic_label: Accrual-based top income shares using Norwegian ownership data
answer.notes: The 2005 tax reform matters mainly because it changed when firms paid out profits, which shifts measured inequality; it is not evaluated as a policy. Author 4 is also listed at Statistics Norway's Research Department, which would be economics.

answer.topic_label: NSF rotators' mentoring spillovers on junior scientists
answer.notes: Grant-success spillovers of the NSF rotation programme on departmental colleagues are coded as unintended (outside the programme's staffing aim); the design compares outcomes before and after a rotator's return against control groups, a difference-in-differences-style comparison.

answer.topic_label: Student debt cancellation and racial wealth gaps
answer.notes: The relief plan was struck down, so the paper simulates the effects of a proposed policy that was never put in place, using an accounting approach.

answer.topic_label: Teacher pay-for-performance: selection and effort in Rwanda
answer.notes: The pay-for-percentile contract is an experimental public-sector pay design tested on civil-servant teachers, so I coded it as a proposed policy; author 3's unit is development studies, coded as other.

answer.topic_label: Corporate finance framing of sovereign debt and money
answer.notes: I coded this presidential address as a research article because it puts forward a new conceptual framework; the cost-benefit flag rests on its discussion of the costs and benefits of inflation and of optimal reserves, which is a weak basis.

answer.topic_label: Export demand shocks and firm innovation
answer.notes: Identification comes from exogenous firm-level export demand shocks, which look like a shift-share design. Authors are coded economics because of PSE, Banque de France and NBER affiliations.

answer.topic_label: Factor momentum explains individual stock momentum
answer.notes: Author 1 has no affiliation; author 2 is coded business school because of the Tuck Hall address and Tuck email.

answer.topic_label: Minimum grade rules for economics majors
answer.notes: The 'policy' is a college's grading rule, which counts as an institution's rule rather than a public policy, so all policy categories are no.

answer.topic_label: Bootstrap standard errors and conservative inference
Manipulability of stable matching mechanisms in large markets
answer.notes: The affiliation names only the university, with no department.

answer.topic_label: Multinationals transmitting business cycle shocks across countries
answer.notes: The paper documents firm-level comovement and then uses a calibrated quantitative model. It does not study a policy.

answer.topic_label: JPE editorial turnaround time statistics
answer.notes: Journal front matter with a table of editorial turnaround times; the abstract field is scraped page text, and no authors are listed.

answer.topic_label: Household car spending in the Great Recession
answer.notes: The recession is a shock, not a policy; descriptive_fact is a yes because the paper documents spending collapses that differ by cohort.

answer.topic_label: Economic epidemiology of infectious disease control
answer.notes: This is a JEL survey; I coded the policy categories from its review of models of epidemic control measures and externalities.

answer.topic_label: Contingent convertible debt design and bank capital structure
answer.notes: The abstract treats contingent convertibles as a security issued by firms, not as a regulatory requirement, so all policy categories are coded no.

answer.topic_label: Earnings reporting responses to pension benefit formulas
answer.notes: The abstract does not name the identification design; I coded it quasi-experimental because the study uses the benefit calculation window as its source of incentive variation. Authors 2 and 3 are coded economics from their CEPR and IZA affiliations.

answer.topic_label: Nonparametric bootstrap for yield curve inference
answer.notes: This is a methods paper with an empirical application on whether bond returns can be predicted.

answer.topic_label: Childhood conflict exposure and asylum seeker crime
answer.notes: The headline result is the effect of conflict exposure, not of a policy; the policy finding relies on differences in integration policy across Swiss regions; author 2's unit (Geneva School of Economics and Management) is ambiguous between economics and business.

answer.topic_label: Idea exchange as agglomeration force in cities
answer.notes: The model is compared with known facts about cities but not estimated on data, so I coded it as theoretical.

answer.topic_label: Credit supply shocks, inventory liquidation and output prices
answer.notes: The Lehman failure is a one-off shock, not a policy, so every policy category is coded no.

answer.topic_label: Teacher student loan forgiveness take-up and value
answer.notes: The paper uses both a quasi-experimental design on eligibility and an RCT of an information intervention; experimental was picked as the main design.

answer.topic_label: Bayesian social learning in networks with changing state
answer.notes: The third author's affiliation is a private firm (Uber), so I coded it as other.

answer.topic_label: Market value of FinTech patent innovations
answer.notes: Stock-price-response valuation is close to an event study, but I coded it as measurement or correlation rather than a causal design.

answer.topic_label: Economic research on what managers do
answer.notes: Annual Review survey that includes a small descriptive look at LinkedIn skills data.

answer.topic_label: Book review: economic crises shaping globalization
answer.notes: Book review in JEL; the abstract only describes the book under review.

answer.topic_label: Unilateral divorce laws and assortative marriage matching
answer.notes: The paper combines staggered state adoption (quasi-experimental) with a structural equilibrium model; the effect on assortative matching was coded as a side effect of divorce law.

answer.topic_label: Mental health effects of elderly COVID curfews
answer.notes: Mental health is treated as a side effect of a curfew meant to limit COVID spread; the mobility decline is the first stage, not reported as a headline policy outcome.

answer.topic_label: Identification and normalizations in skill formation models
answer.notes: The affiliation names only the University of Bonn and no unit; the paper is about identification theory, and any policy relevance is only implied.

answer.topic_label: German Reunification and East German youths' college plans
answer.notes: I treated Reunification as a one-off shift in regime rather than a policy, so every policy category is no.

answer.topic_label: Childhood coca labor and adult criminality in Peru
answer.notes: US antidrug policy timing is the identifying variation; its effects on Peruvian child labour and later crime are coded as unintended consequences, and the CCT's mitigating role is coded as evidence on mechanisms.

answer.topic_label: Hypothesis testing in second-order identified moment models
High-dimensional network model of social media influencers
answer.notes: Author 2 lists several units in different fields (blockchain centre, information science and finance, mathematics, economics), so the discipline is uncertain.

answer.topic_label: Law enforcement, managerial delegation and aggregate productivity
answer.notes: It is unclear whether the strength of law enforcement counts as a policy or as institutional quality; I treated it as a public policy. The model is quantitative and partly calibrated, so the boundary between structural and calibration was a close call.

answer.topic_label: Corporate flexibility and firm plans during COVID
answer.notes: The paper appears to rely on CFO survey data and uses the COVID shock rather than any policy, so the design is coded as correlational; authors 2 and 3 are coded economics because NBER is the only unit named in their affiliations.

answer.topic_label: India's growth without broad-based development
answer.notes: This is a JEP synthesis of India's development patterns; it is unclear whether it includes original descriptive analysis or only reviews existing work.

answer.topic_label: Optimal spatial allocation of cognitive workers across cities
answer.notes: The paper studies an optimal spatial policy that the authors derive inside an estimated spatial equilibrium model; it does not evaluate a policy that actually exists.

answer.topic_label: Incidence of business owner taxes on employee earnings
answer.notes: I coded the pass-through of the tax to employee earnings as a spillover (unintended consequence). I coded the fall in after-tax inequality as the tax's intended effect.

answer.topic_label: Optimal monetary policy and asset price overshooting
answer.notes: Author 2 affiliation is a garbled acknowledgement footnote naming MIT/NBER and Yale SOM/NBER/CEPR; coded as economics on the basis of NBER/CEPR. The paper is mainly theoretical, with a descriptive look at the COVID-19 recovery.

answer.topic_label: Norwegian vocational education reform and social mobility
answer.notes: The wider gender gap in earnings is coded as an unintended consequence; disciplines are coded from the NBER and Statistics Norway affiliations.

answer.topic_label: Classroom peer effects on children's personality traits
answer.notes: The paper identifies peer effects from schools randomly assigning children to classrooms, which I coded as quasi-experimental; peer effects and parental migration are not policies; author 2's unit (digital humanities and computational social sciences) is coded as other.

answer.topic_label: Church attendance effects on crime via rainfall
answer.notes: Uses Sunday rainfall as an instrument for church attendance; no government policy is studied.

answer.topic_label: Bank regulation and capital flow surges and stops
answer.notes: The evidence is correlational. The unintended-consequence finding (macroprudential rules linked to more sudden stops and to leakage outside regulated banks) is suggestive, not causally identified.

answer.topic_label: Low-quality maize seeds, uncertainty and farm returns
answer.notes: The experiment varies seed quality and whether farmers know which seed they got, which is a researcher intervention and not a public policy, so every policy category is no. Wageningen and Flowminder were coded unknown because no department or unit is named.

answer.topic_label: Dynamic bank management and deposit value
answer.notes: Leverage requirements are part of the model and are only discussed in general terms, without a counterfactual policy analysis. The author list looks garbled: entry 2 is a correspondence line for an author at the same school as entry 1, and entry 4 has no affiliation.

answer.topic_label: WTO versus preferential trade agreements
answer.notes: This is a JEL survey that weighs the WTO against PTAs; the welfare code reflects its evaluative conclusion, and authors 1 and 3 are coded economics on the basis of their NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Nineteenth-century mechanization and task-level labor productivity
answer.notes: This JEP piece analyses its own historical data, so it is coded as a research article rather than a survey; the descriptive_fact code depends on how closely the link to the future-of-work debate counts as bearing on policy.

answer.topic_label: Financial sanctions and German bank lending responses
answer.notes: The design is inferred as quasi-experimental because the paper uses sanction imposition as its source of variation; the abstract does not name the method.

answer.topic_label: Inside versus outside collateral and financial fragility
answer.notes: Theoretical model of collateral pyramids in wholesale funding markets; no specific policy is analysed.

answer.topic_label: Widening gender earnings gap over early careers
answer.notes: Author 4's Oslo Institute for Social Research is a multidisciplinary institute, so coding it as sociology_demography is uncertain.

answer.topic_label: Seven centuries of long-term real interest rates
answer.notes: I coded descriptive_fact as yes because the long-run trend in real rates matters for monetary policy, even though the paper studies no specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Unemployment, negative equity and strategic mortgage default
answer.notes: The abstract presents estimated effects of job loss and equity on default without a stated identification strategy, so the design is coded as correlational.

answer.topic_label: Gender differences in student professional networking
answer.notes: The networking website is a private or university platform, not a public policy. The descriptive fact concerns gender gaps in the labour market.

answer.topic_label: Audits distorting public procurement methods in Chile
answer.notes: Author 1 has only the IDB as affiliation, with no unit named, so coding it as economics is uncertain. Author 2 is coded as public policy from the institution's name (National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies).

answer.topic_label: Contrast effects in sequential candidate interviews
answer.notes: The proposed changes to interview design apply to how organisations run admission and hiring, not to public policy, so every policy category is coded no.

answer.topic_label: Mental health peer spillovers among new mothers
answer.notes: The Danish postnatal care programme serves only as the source of as-good-as-random peer assignment, and the finding is a peer effect rather than a policy effect, so all policy categories are no; VIVE is multidisciplinary, so those authors are coded unknown.

answer.topic_label: Monetary tightening, mortgage DTI limits, and distributional effects
answer.notes: The quasi-experimental design is inferred from exposure to the DTI thresholds across loans and regions. Authors 2 and 4 are coded economics because they list NBER alongside a business school. Author 1's FHFA affiliation does not name a unit.

answer.topic_label: Private equity buyouts and workplace injury rates
answer.notes: PE buyouts are private firm decisions, so every policy category is no; the abstract states no identifying design, so I coded it as descriptive, though it may use a matched difference-in-differences.

answer.topic_label: Ending sterilization requirement for legal gender change
answer.notes: The paper compares outcomes before and after the 2013 reform without a clear identification strategy, so I coded it as descriptive; SOFI is a multidisciplinary institute, and I coded it as economics.

answer.topic_label: Firm dynamics with on-the-job search frictions
answer.notes: The abstract doesn't say whether the quantitative model is calibrated or estimated, so I coded it as calibration.

answer.topic_label: Government portfolio choice under social and fiscal risk
answer.notes: Theoretical model that weighs how attractive generic financial stability programs are; no specific real-world policy is evaluated.

answer.topic_label: Racial disparities in small business loan terms
answer.notes: The Public Policy Institute of California affiliation was coded as public policy. The other affiliations name only a university, so those authors are coded unknown.

answer.topic_label: Role model movie and Ugandan students' exam performance
answer.notes: The movie screening was a researcher-run experiment, not a public policy, so all policy categories are coded no.

answer.topic_label: Optimal inflation with incomplete markets and money bubbles
answer.notes: Theoretical model in which the policy studied is the money growth rate (inflation), analysed for its effects on growth and welfare.

answer.topic_label: Mutual fund managers' rational attention allocation over business cycle
answer.notes: Author 1's Imperial unit combines accounting, finance and macroeconomics, so I coded it as finance_accounting.

answer.topic_label: ECB policy spillovers to U.S. Treasury yields
answer.notes: I coded the effect of ECB policy on U.S. yields as a cross-border spillover (unintended_consequences); the study uses high-frequency identification of monetary shocks.

answer.topic_label: Stock return momentum in Imperial Russia
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the fields that depend on the abstract are inferred from the title.

answer.topic_label: Difference-in-differences estimators for dynamic treatment effects
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the abstract-based fields are inferred from it, and CREST-ENSAE is coded as economics.

answer.topic_label: Interconnectedness of banks in the interbank market
answer.notes: Only the title was available; author 2 is coded from the Kogod business school address, and authors 3 and 4 list building addresses with no named unit.

answer.topic_label: Bank cross-selling of loans to household depositors
answer.notes: The paper studies how banks behave, not a policy. Author 1 is coded finance_accounting because the affiliation names the Swiss Finance Institute.

answer.topic_label: Lottery incentives for HIV prevention in Lesotho
answer.notes: I treated the lottery as an experimental public-health programme. Whether the government ran it is not stated, so I coded it as a proposed intervention.

answer.topic_label: AEA Committee on Government Relations report
answer.notes: Only the title was available; this is an AEA committee report, and the affiliation names no unit.

answer.topic_label: Artificial counterfactual method for high-dimensional panels
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the record has no abstract, so the abstract-based fields are inferred from the title.

answer.topic_label: Optimal commodity taxes with non-salient taxes
answer.notes: I coded all three authors as economics because each lists NBER as well as a university that names no department (or Wharton, a business school).

answer.topic_label: Long-run interest rate elasticity of microcredit demand
answer.notes: The interest-rate variation was set by a private microlender (Compartamos), so it is not a policy; authors were coded economics because their affiliations include NBER/J-PAL, though they list several institutions.

answer.topic_label: Management practices and firm export performance
answer.notes: The paper combines matched firm data and an RCT in India, but the headline results are correlations; the management intervention is not a government policy.

answer.topic_label: Statutory retirement ages as reference points
answer.notes: The design combines bunching at pension discontinuities, which is quasi-experimental, with structural bunching estimation; I coded it structural because the headline reference-point estimates come from that step.

answer.topic_label: Survey of offshoring effects on labor markets
answer.notes: Authors 1 and 2 are coded economics from their NBER and IZA affiliations; author 3 lists only Purdue University, so the discipline is unknown.

answer.topic_label: Dealer insurance, market structure and market liquidity
answer.notes: Only the title was available; research type guessed as theoretical, and author 2 was coded economics because the BIS is listed first among several affiliations.

answer.topic_label: Rational inattention and menu costs in multi-product pricing
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the design and the other abstract-based fields are inferred from the title.

answer.topic_label: Return migration, skill investment and immigrant wages
answer.notes: The migration-policy analysis appears to be counterfactual simulation of residence restrictions; it is unclear whether these mirror existing policies. Authors are coded economics because their affiliations name economics research centres (IGIER, CReAM).

answer.topic_label: Oil sector indigenization, corruption and theft in Nigeria
answer.notes: The abstract does not name the identification design, so quasi_experimental is my inference from the comparison of local and foreign firms' output under the indigenization policy.

answer.topic_label: Meritocracy, group identity and affirmative action in selection
answer.notes: The policy coding is uncertain. Group-contingent selection is partly set by institutions (university admissions rules), but it is also shaped by public policy (state referenda, legal rules); the paper is coded as explaining mechanisms behind affirmative-action efficiency effects.

answer.topic_label: Effectiveness of stock market trading pauses
answer.notes: Only the title was available; treated trading pauses (circuit breakers) as regulatory policy, though they may be exchange-set rules.

answer.topic_label: Optimal confidence intervals for regression functionals
answer.notes: Methods paper with only an illustrative empirical application; no author affiliations given.

answer.topic_label: Sensitivity of structural counterfactuals to distributional assumptions
answer.notes: This is a methods paper with illustrative structural applications. Author 2 works at a private trading firm, which I coded as finance_accounting.

answer.topic_label: Bank branch expansion, financial access, and inequality in Thailand
answer.notes: The micro estimates come from branch openings, which are bank decisions, so causal_effect_of_policy is coded no; the policy findings rest on modelled deregulation and counterfactual subsidies.

answer.topic_label: Perturbation algorithm for solving large macroeconomic models
answer.notes: This is a numerical solution method rather than a statistical one; I coded it as econometric_methods because that is the closest available category.

answer.topic_label: Uncertainty in Federal Reserve output gap estimates
answer.notes: Fed staff output gap estimates are a measurement input to policy rather than a policy, so descriptive_fact is the only policy category coded yes.

answer.topic_label: Fairness concerns, price rigidity and monetary nonneutrality
answer.notes: Theoretical New Keynesian model; the mechanisms code rests on a fairness-based explanation of why monetary policy affects output, not on an evaluation of a specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Managers learning from market reactions to capex forecasts
answer.notes: Voluntary disclosure is a firm decision, not a public policy.

answer.topic_label: American Finance Association secretary-treasurer annual report
answer.notes: Only the title was available; this is an association's administrative report, and no authors are listed.

answer.topic_label: Robot-labor substitution elasticity and occupational wages
answer.notes: The paper estimates parameters of a general equilibrium model with a model-implied instrument (it could also be read as quasi-experimental IV); its call for "targeted policy" is general and names no specific policy.

answer.topic_label: Inference for estimators from mathematical programming
answer.notes: Only the title was available; Amazon gives no named unit, and Caltech's Humanities and Social Sciences division is a mixed unit coded as other.

answer.topic_label: Regression discontinuity methods for categorical outcomes
answer.notes: Only the title was available; abstract-based fields are inferred from it.

answer.topic_label: Cyclical income risk and life-cycle portfolio choice
answer.notes: Affiliation names only the Wharton School with no department, so it is coded as business_management.

answer.topic_label: Lender of last resort policy uncertainty and real economy
answer.notes: Only the title was available; research type and policy fields are guesses based on the title.

answer.topic_label: Persistence of individual wages over time
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the panel-data econometrics reading is inferred from the journal.

answer.topic_label: Expulsion of Jewish managers and firm performance
answer.notes: The abstract presents the expulsions as the result of rising discrimination, not of a specific state policy, so all policy categories are coded no; this is borderline because Aryanization was partly state-driven.

answer.topic_label: Buy Now, Pay Later effects on merchants
answer.notes: Only the title was available; the research type and empirical design are guesses, and author 4 is coded economics because of the NBER affiliation.

answer.topic_label: Retail chain uniform pricing spreads local demand shocks
answer.notes: Uniform pricing is a firm decision, not a policy, so all policy categories are no. The design uses house-price demand shocks passed through chain networks and adds a model-based counterfactual, so it sits between quasi-experimental and structural.

answer.topic_label: Data availability and information in financial markets
answer.notes: Only the title was available, so the topic, JEL code and design are guesses; authors 3 and 4 also hold economics affiliations (NBER, Minneapolis Fed).
